abstract: Corrosion and flow-induced erosion of metallic infrastructure impose an estimated US$2.5 trillion annual global burden and constitute leading causes of catastrophic failure across nuclear waste transport, oil and gas transmission, marine, and civil sectors. Automated visual inspection has advanced through convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs), yet each family alone is insufficient: CNNs capture local texture but struggle with global context, while ViTs model long-range dependencies but are texture-insensitive and data-hungry. Prior hybrid designs rely on static feature concatenation, forfeiting adaptive cross-modal interaction, and typically address binary rather than mechanism-differentiated classification. Here we present CorroSense-Net, a hybrid CNN–Transformer framework that couples a ResNet-50 branch and a ViT-B/16 branch through a novel Cross-Attention Fusion (CAF) module performing bidirectional gated attention between the two streams. The framework classifies industrial pipeline imagery into three physically grounded states—pristine, particle-impingement erosion, and chemical corrosion— and integrates Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification and quantitative Grad-CAM interpretability scored against expert annotations. We developed and validated the framework on 487 smartphone-captured images from two purpose-built laboratory rigs reproducing nuclear-waste-transport degradation mechanisms, with ultrasonic thickness measurements providing independent label verification. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation, CorroSense-Net achieved a macro-F1 of 0.961 ± 0.014 and ROC-AUC of 0.991 ± 0.006, outperforming ResNet-50, ViT-B/16, EfficientNet-B3, Swin-Tiny, and the concatenation-based hybrid HCT-Net by statistically significant margins after Bonferroni correction. Cross-Attention Fusion improved Grad-CAM alignment with expert masks by 7.5 IoU percentage points over concatenation-based fusion, and zero-shot inference on two public datasets confirmed cross-domain generalization. The framework establishes a template for interpretable, uncertainty-aware AI in safety-critical industrial inspection.
title: Interpretable Hybrid CNN Transformer Framework with Cross Attention Fusion and Uncertainty Quantification for Multi Mechanism Corrosion and Erosion Detection
